props.title: 13 Ghosts

sections.content: William Castle's 13 Ghosts (1960) pioneered gimmick-driven horror cinema with "Illusion-O" - special glasses audiences used to see or "remove" ghosts from the screen. This groundbreaking theatrical trick exemplified Castle's showmanship, following his success with House on Haunted Hill (1959) and its "Emergo" floating skeleton. The film's plot about a family inheriting a haunted mansion from an eccentric occultist uncle established tropes that influenced later haunted house films like The Amityville Horror (1979) and Poltergeist (1982).

sections.content: Castle's influence on horror marketing and audience participation can't be overstated. His theatrical gimmicks spawned imitators like Percepto! in The Tingler (1959) where theater seats vibrated during key scenes. John Waters, heavily influenced by Castle, paid homage with Polyester (1981) using "Odorama" scratch-and-sniff cards. Modern films like Ready or Not (2019) and Escape Room (2019) continue Castle's tradition of turning horror into participatory entertainment.

The original 13 Ghosts showcases early practical effects and creative use of color filters, techniques that influenced later supernatural films. Its 2001 remake Thir13en Ghosts amplified the original's concept with modern CGI but lost Castle's playful audience interaction. The original's family-friendly approach to horror, balancing scares with humor, created a template followed by films like The Monster Squad (1987) and Casper (1995). SUBHEAD: The Legacy of William Castle's Horror Showmanship

sections.content: Castle's marketing genius extended beyond 13 Ghosts. For Macabre (1958), he offered audience members life insurance policies in case they died of fright. This carnival barker approach to horror marketing influenced everything from The Blair Witch Project's (1999) found footage campaign to Paranormal Activity's (2007) "Demand It!" screening strategy. Modern horror producers like Jason Blum have cited Castle's promotional innovations as inspiration for their own marketing approaches.
